LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 HANDWRITING / BRAILLE WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting / Braille writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting / Braille writing, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we identify lowercase letters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting / Braille writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: The learner self-discipline is enhanced when practising correct letter formation and writing from left to right.

Values:
Unity is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers to practises shaping letters correctly

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self- esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is enhanced as they are able to shape or form the letters of the alphabet correctly.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies the writing skills to when writing materials in all the learning areas.

Suggested learning resources

• Models,

• Chart in appropriate font and colour contrast,

• Pattern books,

• Tactile boards and charts

• Braille letter cards

• Textbooks in print and in braille
